question: How can a tele-nurse help assess a patient's physical status from afar?

options.A: Guessing the vital signs based on the patient's age
options.B: Relying entirely on laboratory tests done once a year
options.C: Guiding the patient or caregiver to perform simple checks at home
options.D: Physically walking to the patient's house for every assessment

explanation: You got it! You can coach the patient or a family member on how to check simple things like pulse rate or swelling at home.

question: A family caregiver looks completely exhausted, can't sleep, and feels hopeless. What should be your very first nursing move?

options.A: Hand them a prescription for antidepressants right there in the clinic
options.B: Suggest respite care options and connect them with social work services
options.C: Tell them to ignore the patient and travel abroad
options.D: Tell them not to worry because things always work out

explanation: Caregivers need care too! When exhaustion hits this hard, they need backup like respite care and professional social work support.

question: What is the primary goal of health education?

options.A: Empowering people to improve their health
options.B: Dispensing free pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Enforcing hospital administrative policies
options.D: Diagnosing rare tropical diseases

explanation: Health education focuses on giving individuals and communities the knowledge and tools they need to improve their own health outcomes. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h1)

question: What do altmetrics mainly track when measuring how far a research study has traveled?

options.A: How many patients refuse to take their prescribed pills
options.B: Social media mentions and online news coverage
options.C: The exact cost of printing paper hospital posters
options.D: The number of physical books sold in university shops

explanation: You got it! Altmetrics look at online buzz, like shares on social media, blogs, and news platforms.

question: What is the first step in the risk management process?

options.A: Patient discharge
options.B: Risk identification
options.C: Staff punishment
options.D: Financial compensation

explanation: You cannot manage a hazard until you first find out it exists by spotting it through reports, audits, or observation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which type of foetal skull injury generally heals spontaneously without causing permanent neurological damage?

options.A: Extensive subdural hematoma
options.B: Severe subgaleal hemorrhage
options.C: Simple linear fracture
options.D: Depressed fracture with brain compression

explanation: Simple linear fractures are closed and stable, usually healing on their own without requiring surgical intervention or leaving lasting deficits. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h6)

question: Why is throwing away medical waste improperly such a big danger to people living outside the hospital?

options.A: It immediately increases the cost of municipal electricity bills
options.B: It can contaminate local water supplies and soil with pathogens and chemicals
options.C: It triggers loud community noise pollution during night hours
options.D: It causes immediate structural damage to residential homes

explanation: When hazardous waste isn't contained properly, dangerous germs and chemicals can leak into the soil and water where the local community lives and farms. Safety starts with proper disposal!

question: Why are Infant Welfare Clinics usually set up right inside primary health care centres?

options.A: To provide specialized pediatric surgery units
options.B: To isolate sick children from the general population
options.C: To bring preventive services closer to local communities
options.D: To reduce the workload of tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Placing clinics in local primary health care centres brings essential services right to the grassroots, making it super easy for families to attend routine check-ups.

question: A nurse accidentally drops and breaks an old mercury blood pressure machine on the ward floor. What kind of hazard is this?

options.A: Chemical hazard
options.B: Biological hazard
options.C: Genotoxic hazard
options.D: Radioactive hazard

explanation: Mercury is a toxic heavy metal, making it a chemical hazard. Its vapors can easily be breathed in or absorbed through the skin if not cleaned up properly!

question: How does the tongue help us speak clearly and pronounce words?

options.A: By controlling the rate of air expelled from the lungs
options.B: By opening and closing the lips to form consonants
options.C: By generating vocal cord vibrations in the pharynx
options.D: By altering its shape and position to interrupt and shape oral airflow

explanation: Our tongue is amazingly nimble—it taps against our teeth and palate to turn breath into clear speech and sounds!

question: Why do quantitative researchers try to remain completely neutral and detached from their study participants?

options.A: To avoid having to write detailed nursing care plans
options.B: To prevent personal bias from affecting the study results
options.C: To make it easier to recruit busy hospital staff
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of running the project

explanation: Staying objective ensures the data truly reflects reality, rather than what the researcher hopes or wishes to see.

question: Which of these is actually helpful and NOT a barrier to hand hygiene on a busy ward?

options.A: Lack of skin moisturizers
options.B: Readily available sanitizer dispensers
options.C: Heavy patient workloads
options.D: Hand irritation and dermatitis

explanation: When sanitizers are placed right where you need them, it's so much easier to clean your hands on the go!

question: How can Nigerian nurses break through barriers that keep them out of health planning rooms?

options.A: By ignoring hospital management and making independent laws
options.B: By working entirely in private clinics without government oversight
options.C: By building strong professional advocacy and gaining leadership training
options.D: By refusing to care for patients until they are given management titles

explanation: Brilliant! Standing up for our profession, sharpening our leadership skills, and bringing solid evidence helps us earn our rightful seat at the table.

question: Why do intersectoral teams sometimes struggle to communicate with each other?

options.A: Nurses refuse to share office space with workers from other government departments
options.B: Government policies legally forbid workers from different ministries from talking
options.C: Different professional sectors use unique terminology and focus on different priorities
options.D: Community leaders only communicate through written memos in foreign languages

explanation: Exactly! Every profession has its own special terms. If we don't use simple, shared language, misunderstandings happen easily.

question: Why can treating quarantine rules with harsh, heavy-handed punishments actually backfire?

options.A: It forces public health nurses to resign from their clinical positions
options.B: It costs too much money for hospital laboratories to process test kits
options.C: It drives infected people to hide their symptoms and avoid testing out of fear
options.D: It increases the biological mutation rate of the infectious pathogen

explanation: Spot on. If people are terrified of harsh penalties or stigma, they will hide their sickness instead of seeking help, making the outbreak worse.

question: What is the main goal of conducting a community health assessment?

options.A: To gather data on population health needs and available resources
options.B: To close down clinics that do not meet modern standards
options.C: To prescribe individual drugs to every household member
options.D: To punish local leaders for poor sanitation practices

explanation: Spot on! Before a nurse can help a community, they must first find out what problems exist and what resources are already available.

question: Why must a woman with an intact uterus take progesterone along with estrogen replacement therapy?

options.A: To stop the ovaries from producing any remaining androgens
options.B: To eliminate the risk of developing hot flashes
options.C: To prevent the development of high blood pressure
options.D: To prevent the buildup of the uterine lining and lower the risk of cancer

explanation: Estrogen alone can cause the uterine lining to grow too thick, raising cancer risks. Adding progesterone keeps the lining safe and balanced!

question: Which of these common infections spreads mainly through direct skin-to-skin touch?

options.A: Scabies
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Tuberculosis
options.D: Tetanus

explanation: Scabies is caused by tiny mites that love to crawl from one person's skin straight onto another during close contact. Easy peasy!

question: What is the primary difference between monitoring and evaluation in nutrition programs?

options.A: Monitoring tracks ongoing activities, while evaluation measures long-term impact
options.B: Monitoring is done by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring only happens once a decade
options.D: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is always free

explanation: Monitoring watches day-to-day progress, whereas evaluation looks at the final outcomes and overall success of the intervention. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h8)

question: What does client-centered care focus on the most when dealing with reproductive health?

options.A: The traditional beliefs of the senior medical doctors
options.B: The rigid scheduling needs of the hospital administration
options.C: The personal preferences and autonomy of the individual
options.D: The financial targets set by the facility management

explanation: Brilliant! Client-centered care puts the patient in the driver's seat, respecting their personal choices and rights over their own body. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is inter-sectorial collaboration in disaster management?

options.A: The independent operation of government ministries without outside help
options.B: The complete takeover of local clinics by the military during crises
options.C: The coordinated pooling of skills and resources by different agencies
options.D: The exclusive funding of emergency hospitals by private businesses

explanation: Think of it like group work in class—different agencies team up and share what they have to handle emergencies smoothly!

question: A patient has a heart rate of 180 beats per minute, low blood pressure, and acute chest pain. What is the immediate treatment priority?

options.A: Starting continuous chest compressions
options.B: Synchronized cardioversion
options.C: Oral beta-blocker pills
options.D: Waiting for blood lab results

explanation: An unstable fast rhythm causing low blood pressure and chest pain requires immediate synchronized electrical cardioversion. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h6)

question: How does psychoeducation benefit families of clients with mental health conditions?

options.A: It legally transfers all medical responsibility away from the healthcare team
options.B: It empowers them with knowledge about the illness and how to handle crises effectively
options.C: It completely eliminates all stressful events from their household
options.D: It teaches them how to diagnose and prescribe psychiatric drugs independently

explanation: When families understand the condition and recognize early warning signs, they can provide supportive care and prevent emergency situations. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is classified as Type IV FGM?

options.A: Excising the prepuce of the clitoris only
options.B: Suturing the vaginal opening completely shut
options.C: Removing both the clitoris and labia minora
options.D: Piercing the clitoris or labia

explanation: Type IV covers other harmful practices like pricking, piercing, scraping, or cauterizing the female genitalia without medical reasons.

question: Why do clinics use more than one test (an algorithm) instead of just one rapid test for a positive result?

options.A: To make the testing process longer and more thorough
options.B: To ensure diagnostic accuracy and prevent misdiagnosis
options.C: To use up excess laboratory supplies before they expire
options.D: To comply with insurance billing requirements for hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Running sequential tests confirms initial results so we protect clients from the heavy emotional blow of a false positive.

question: Why do we need a team of different professionals in palliative care?

options.A: Hospital regulations require at least ten staff members per patient.
options.B: No single profession can address all physical, emotional, and spiritual needs.
options.C: Nurses only handle administrative paperwork in palliative settings.
options.D: Doctors are not allowed to talk to family members directly.

explanation: No single person knows it all! Caring for someone with a serious illness takes doctors, nurses, social workers, and spiritual leaders all working hand-in-hand to cover every angle.

question: Which induration measurement is considered positive for a patient with no known risk factors for tuberculosis?

options.A: 15 millimeters or more
options.B: 5 millimeters or more
options.C: 10 millimeters or more
options.D: 20 millimeters or more

explanation: For healthy individuals with no known exposure risks, the cut-off threshold for a positive test is 15 millimeters or greater. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h6)

question: How do simple antacids neutralize extra stomach acid without using cell receptors?

options.A: Through direct chemical neutralization
options.B: By binding to specialized membrane enzymes
options.C: By blocking hormone production in the liver
options.D: Through osmotic drawing of fluid into cells

explanation: Not all drugs need receptors! Antacids simply mix with the stomach acid in a direct chemical reaction to calm things down right away.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when a patient arrives with sudden, severe breathlessness?

options.A: Ask the patient to walk around the room
options.B: Draw blood for a full blood count
options.C: Administer oral bronchodilators immediately
options.D: Assess the airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: ABC! Always check Airway, Breathing, and Circulation first in any emergency. Safety and stabilization come before anything else.

question: An older client with dementia relies totally on her son for baths and medication. Why is she at high risk for abuse?

options.A: She is exposed to many different community health workers daily
options.B: She has financial independence from her family
options.C: Her physical and cognitive dependence creates a severe power imbalance
options.D: Older adults are naturally immune to domestic coercion

explanation: Exactly. When a patient depends completely on just one person for basic daily needs, it opens the door wide to potential abuse.

question: When a severe flood hits a local community, the local Red Cross branch rushes in to set up emergency shelters. What do we call this local branch?

options.A: The ICRC leadership
options.B: A United Nations agency
options.C: A National Society
options.D: A military medical unit

explanation: Spot on! National Societies work right inside their own countries, stepping up as local heroes when disasters strike.

question: How does the high humidity inside a steam tent help a patient with a heavy cough?

options.A: It dilates the tiny air sacs in the lower lungs
options.B: It kills bacterial infections in the upper airway
options.C: It numbs the throat nerves to stop the cough reflex
options.D: It liquefies thick mucus so it is easier to clear

explanation: Spot on! Moisture acts like magic on sticky mucus, thinning it out so the patient can cough it up easily.

question: What are the three main categories of immune system dysregulation?

options.A: Phagocytosis, inflammation, and complement activation
options.B: Hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, and immunodeficiency
options.C: Anaphylaxis, thrombosis, and necrosis
options.D: Antibody production, cellular immunity, and innate defense

explanation: Immune system dysregulation broadly breaks down into overreaction, attacking self-tissues, and underperformance. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why do we need special care when doing research with vulnerable groups?

options.A: To prevent exploitation and protect them from harm
options.B: Because they always pay large amounts of money
options.C: To satisfy international tourism guidelines
options.D: So the researcher can finish data collection quickly

explanation: Vulnerable patients need extra protection because they might easily feel pressured to agree to a study. Keeping them safe is our top priority.

question: What is the primary goal of nursing informatics in clinical practice?

options.A: To manage health data to improve patient care
options.B: To increase the cost of medical equipment
options.C: To reduce the number of hospital administrators
options.D: To replace bedside nurses with automated systems

explanation: The core purpose of informatics is organizing and utilizing data, knowledge, and wisdom to support better clinical decisions and patient outcomes. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which hormone is produced by the Leydig cells in the testes?

options.A: Testosterone
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Great job! The Leydig cells are responsible for making testosterone, which is the main male sex hormone. You've got this!

question: Which sign might tell you that a patient is struggling during a ventilator weaning trial?

options.A: Sweating and an increasing heart rate
options.B: Asking for a glass of cold water
options.C: Calm facial expression and steady sleep
options.D: Lower blood pressure and normal breathing

explanation: If a patient breaks out in a sweat (diaphoresis) and their heart rate spikes, it's a clear distress signal telling us the breathing workload is still too heavy for them.

question: Which body membrane lines closed internal cavities that do NOT open to the outside?

options.A: Synovial membrane
options.B: Mucous membrane
options.C: Serous membrane
options.D: Cutaneous membrane

explanation: Serous membranes line closed cavities like your chest and abdomen, making a slippery fluid to cut down friction.

question: Which study type compares patients who have a specific illness with those who don't, checking to see what they were exposed to in the past?

options.A: Case-control study
options.B: Prospective cohort
options.C: Randomized experiment
options.D: Clinical trial

explanation: You've got this! A case-control study starts with the final outcome (like having the disease) and looks backward to compare who was exposed to a risk factor and who wasn't.

question: Which group of professionals is most ideal for creating a complete care plan for a special needs child?

options.A: Only traditional spiritual healers
options.B: A multidisciplinary team including nurses, therapists, and social workers
options.C: Only hospital accountants and security guards
options.D: Exclusive teams of pharmaceutical sales reps

explanation: Special needs touch on health, education, and social life, so working together in a multidisciplinary team gives the child the best possible holistic care.

question: How can task-shifting help improve community-based mental health care in resource-limited settings?

options.A: By replacing all hospitals with commercial pharmacies
options.B: By stopping nurses from providing care so only doctors can work
options.C: By transferring all psychiatric patients out of the country for treatment
options.D: By training general community health workers to perform basic mental health tasks under supervision

explanation: Task-shifting expands the workforce by equipping local health staff to handle routine follow-ups and education, easing the burden on scarce specialists. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h7)

question: What position is the patient usually placed in during a sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: Left lateral (Sims') position
options.B: Flat on their back (supine)
options.C: Sitting upright in a high chair
options.D: Flat on their stomach (prone)

explanation: You got it! Lying on the left side (Sims' position) naturally aligns the lower bowel, making the scope easier and safer to insert.
